findings.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Legacy-write goroutines derive their ctx from the request ctx, which the k8s handler cancels (deferred cancel) as soon as the response is written, so async legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection are routinely aborted; context.WithoutCancel is needed (same at lines 110, 135, 163)

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Independent unordered per-request goroutines let legacy writes land out of order (e.g. Update/Delete before the preceding Create), so legacy drifts or deleted objects come back, and legacy is still the source of truth if the mode is downgraded

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Legacy Update gets the raw objInfo, so the patch/transform and admission are re-run against legacy's own old object instead of the unified result `res`; this drops the updateWrapper protection the previous code had and can write a different object to legacy

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:161 — Async legacy DeleteCollection can run after later Creates have already landed in legacy, wiping rows that still exist in unified storage (a mass-divergence cascade)

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Unified Create failure is recorded via recordLegacyDuration, so unified-storage error series stay green while legacy dashboards show phantom failures (same bug for Update at line 129)

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — Legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded via recordStorageDuration, so legacy failures show up as unified-storage errors and the legacy series never records delete-collection

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Successful unified Delete passes the object `name` instead of options.Kind as the kind label, which creates an unbounded per-object metric series (cardinality explosion) and puts it in the wrong series

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:56 — Async legacy write errors are never logged, only folded into a histogram label, so legacy divergence is effectively silent with no object name or error to diagnose (same at lines 113, 140, 166)

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:101 — The IsNotFound tolerance on unified Delete was removed, so an object whose earlier async legacy delete failed can never be removed from legacy by retrying (unified returns NotFound first) and it comes back on mode downgrade

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Every write spawns an untracked goroutine that can live up to 10s with no concurrency limit or backpressure, so a slow or hung legacy DB under load piles up unbounded goroutines and DB connections, and Destroy() at line 172 does not wait for in-flight legacy writes

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:53 — Legacy and unified mocks share the same *mock.Mock, so tests cannot tell which store was called; the "unified store fails" Create case (line 38) passes only because the legacy expectation is what makes unified storage fail

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:63 — Tests never wait for the goroutines or call AssertExpectations/AssertCalled on legacy, and never check metrics, so they pass even if legacy writes never happen or land in the wrong metric series

pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:132 — The mode-3 integration tests' "legacy API" checks go through the k8s dual writer (reading from unified in mode 3), since legacy-created playlists must appear in unified storage for the test to pass, so they never verify that async legacy SQL writes landed

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:38 — options.Kind is the options TypeMeta (e.g. "CreateOptions"/"DeleteOptions", or empty), not the resource kind, so the metric and log "kind" labels cannot tell resources apart
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts the bare d.Log into ctx instead of the enriched `log`, dropping name/kind/method from downstream and legacy-goroutine logs

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Async legacy goroutines (also lines 110, 135, 163) derive their context from the request ctx, which is canceled when the handler returns, so legacy writes are likely aborted with context canceled; needs context.WithoutCancel(ctx).
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Create records a unified-storage failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, so it attributes the error to the wrong backend.
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Update records a unified-storage failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — The DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records its result with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, which pollutes storage metrics with legacy timings and errors.
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Successful Delete passes the object name instead of options.Kind as the kind label, giving the wrong label and unbounded metric cardinality.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:134 — Each write starts its own unordered fire-and-forget legacy goroutine, so back-to-back operations on one object (create then delete, update then update) can reach legacy out of order and leave it permanently diverged.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts the bare d.Log into ctx instead of the enriched log, dropping name/kind/method from downstream logging.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Legacy write errors in the async goroutines (also lines 112, 139, 165) are never logged, only counted in a metric, so legacy/unified divergence is silent (the previous code logged them).

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:101 — Delete no longer tolerates NotFound from unified storage, so it skips the legacy delete and leaves legacy-only objects orphaned (the previous code continued to the legacy delete).

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:37 — Per-method `var method = "..."` should be a const, and method naming is inconsistent ("delete-collection" label vs "legacy deletecollection timeout" cause).
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:145 — The List test case name still says the store "is not implemented" even though List is now implemented.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:40 — The unified-store failure case configures its error through setupLegacyFn; because legacy and storage share one mock.Mock, the setup names are misleading and the tests cannot tell which store was called.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:337 — Tests never wait for or assert the async legacy goroutine calls, so the new async-legacy-write behavior is unverified and goroutines can outlive the test.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Async legacy writes derive their context from the request ctx, which is canceled as soon as the handler returns, so legacy Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection (lines 51, 110, 135, 163) are routinely aborted and the 10s timeout never effectively applies (use context.WithoutCancel).

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:56 — Legacy write errors in all goroutines (56, 113, 140, 166) are silently dropped with no log (previous code logged them) and never retried or reconciled, so the stores diverge with no signal beyond a metric.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Background goroutines have no recover(), so a panic in a legacy storage call is outside the apiserver panic-recovery handler and crashes the whole server process.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:110 — Legacy and unified mocks share one *mock.Mock with identical method names, so the "only in unified store" Get/List/Delete tests would still pass if Mode3 read from or wrote to LegacyStorage instead; no AssertNotCalled or per-store distinction exists.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — The legacy goroutines derive their context from the request ctx, which is cancelled once the handler returns, but every test passes context.Background(), so legacy writes being cancelled after the response goes untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Legacy-write goroutines derive their ctx from the request ctx, which the k8s handler cancels (deferred cancel) as soon as the response is written, so async legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection are routinely aborted; context.WithoutCancel is needed (same at lines 110, 135, 163)

adjudication.rationale: In Mode3 Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection, the legacy write is done asynchronously in a goroutine that derives its context from the request ctx (e.g., `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection(ctx, ...) }()`). Since this ctx is the same one passed into the handler (only wrapped with `klog.NewContext`, which preserves cancellation), when the request finishes and the handler cancels the request context, these goroutines can be routinely canceled before completing, aborting the intended async legacy write. The diff shows no use of `context.WithoutCancel` or any other detachment mechanism, so the finding is grounded in the introduced async behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Independent unordered per-request goroutines let legacy writes land out of order (e.g. Update/Delete before the preceding Create), so legacy drifts or deleted objects come back, and legacy is still the source of truth if the mode is downgraded

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes are now performed asynchronously in independent goroutines (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection spawn `go func() { ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) }()` after the unified-store write). Because these goroutines are not ordered or synchronized per object/key, a subsequent request (e.g., Update or Delete) can enqueue/execute its legacy goroutine before the preceding Create’s legacy goroutine runs, leading to out-of-order operations and legacy drift. This is directly implied by the diff’s change from synchronous legacy calls to fire-and-forget goroutines with timeouts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Legacy Update gets the raw objInfo, so the patch/transform and admission are re-run against legacy's own old object instead of the unified result `res`; this drops the updateWrapper protection the previous code had and can write a different object to legacy

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, the Update path was changed from computing the updated object once (via UpdatedObject against the unified-store "old"), then passing an updateWrapper with the unified result into Legacy.Update, to now calling Legacy.Update asynchronously with the original objInfo (`d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)`). This means legacy will re-run objInfo’s transformation/patch logic against legacy’s own pre-update object (and any validation/admission hooked to that path), which can produce a different object than the unified store result `res` and defeats the previous updateWrapper protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:161 — Async legacy DeleteCollection can run after later Creates have already landed in legacy, wiping rows that still exist in unified storage (a mass-divergence cascade)

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the unified store deletion is done synchronously, but the legacy deletion is kicked off asynchronously in a goroutine with no ordering/serialization against other legacy async writes (`Create`, `Update`, `Delete` are also async). This allows an interleaving where `DeleteCollection` (legacy) executes after a subsequent `Create`/`Update` has already been applied to legacy, causing the later object(s) to be deleted from legacy while they still exist in unified storage—i.e., divergence/data loss in legacy. The diff explicitly introduces this async legacy `DeleteCollection` (`go func() { ... d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...) }()`), so the race described is grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Unified Create failure is recorded via recordLegacyDuration, so unified-storage error series stay green while legacy dashboards show phantom failures (same bug for Update at line 129)

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, when `d.Storage.Create(...)` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though the measured operation is the unified `Storage` call (note `startStorage` is used). This misattributes storage failures to the legacy metrics and fails to mark storage error series. The same issue exists in `DualWriterMode3.Update`: on `d.Storage.Update(...)` error it calls `recordLegacyDuration(..., startStorage)` instead of recording a storage duration/error. This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — Legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded via recordStorageDuration, so legacy failures show up as unified-storage errors and the legacy series never records delete-collection
matched_golden_ids: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug in DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection: the wrong metrics recording function/recorder is used, causing legacy vs unified-storage delete-collection durations/failures to be attributed to the wrong series (legacy failures showing up under storage and/or legacy series not recording correctly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Successful unified Delete passes the object `name` instead of options.Kind as the kind label, which creates an unbounded per-object metric series (cardinality explosion) and puts it in the wrong series

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:56 — Async legacy write errors are never logged, only folded into a histogram label, so legacy divergence is effectively silent with no object name or error to diagnose (same at lines 113, 140, 166)

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, legacy writes are moved into goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). In each async block the returned error (e.g., `errObjectSt` / `err`) is only used to call `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` and is never logged (no `log.Error(...)` or similar). Previously, legacy failures were logged synchronously (e.g., old Create logged `unable to create object in legacy storage`; old Delete/DeleteCollection logged non-NotFound errors). This diff therefore makes legacy-write failures largely silent aside from metrics, reducing diagnosability (and for Create/DeleteCollection the async log context also doesn’t include object name).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:101 — The IsNotFound tolerance on unified Delete was removed, so an object whose earlier async legacy delete failed can never be removed from legacy by retrying (unified returns NotFound first) and it comes back on mode downgrade

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the previous implementation tolerated `IsNotFound` from the unified store delete (storage) and would still attempt `Legacy.Delete` (only returning early for non-NotFound errors). The new code returns early on *any* error from `d.Storage.Delete` and only schedules the legacy delete goroutine on success. This means if unified storage returns NotFound (e.g., legacy still has the object due to an earlier async legacy delete failing), retries will never clean up legacy, matching the finding’s scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Every write spawns an untracked goroutine that can live up to 10s with no concurrency limit or backpressure, so a slow or hung legacy DB under load piles up unbounded goroutines and DB connections, and Destroy() at line 172 does not wait for in-flight legacy writes

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now launch legacy writes in `go func() { ... }` with a 10s timeout (e.g., Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection), but there is no semaphore/worker pool, no tracking (no WaitGroup), and no backpressure. Under load, slow legacy operations could accumulate many concurrent goroutines and in-flight legacy calls. The diff also shows `Destroy()` exists but no mechanism is added to wait/cancel these goroutines, so shutdown can’t coordinate in-flight legacy writes. This is a concrete scalability/operational concern introduced by the change, though it may be an intentional best-effort async design rather than a strict correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:53 — Legacy and unified mocks share the same *mock.Mock, so tests cannot tell which store was called; the "unified store fails" Create case (line 38) passes only because the legacy expectation is what makes unified storage fail

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go the tests instantiate a single testify *mock.Mock (m := &mock.Mock{}) and wrap it in both legacyStoreMock{m, l} and storageMock{m, s}. Expectations are set on method names like "Create" without distinguishing legacy vs unified storage. In the "error when creating object in the unified store fails" case, only a legacy expectation is configured (m.On("Create", ..., failingObj, ...).Return(nil, error)), but DualWriter mode3 calls Storage.Create first; that call can match and consume the legacy expectation because it’s the same mock and same method name/args, making the test pass for the wrong reason and preventing the test from accurately asserting which store was called.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:63 — Tests never wait for the goroutines or call AssertExpectations/AssertCalled on legacy, and never check metrics, so they pass even if legacy writes never happen or land in the wrong metric series

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy operations in Mode3 are executed asynchronously via `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection ... }()`. In the new `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` tests, the mocks set up `m.On(...)` for legacy calls in some cases (e.g., `TestMode3_Create`/`Update`), but the tests never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` / `AssertCalled`, nor do they wait for those goroutines to run before the test ends. As a result, the tests primarily validate unified-store return values and can pass even if legacy writes never occur or if metrics aren’t recorded/are recorded under wrong labels (metrics are not asserted anywhere). This is a concrete test-coverage/verification gap introduced by the async legacy writes, not a direct functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:132 — The mode-3 integration tests' "legacy API" checks go through the k8s dual writer (reading from unified in mode 3), since legacy-created playlists must appear in unified storage for the test to pass, so they never verify that async legacy SQL writes landed

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows new mode-3 integration test cases in pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go that call doPlaylistTests with different GrafanaOpts, but it does not show what “legacy API checks” exist inside doPlaylistTests or how they validate legacy SQL writes. While pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go does read only from Storage (unified) and performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines, the specific claim that the playlist mode-3 integration tests “never verify that async legacy SQL writes landed” cannot be verified from the provided diff because the relevant assertions/logic are not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:38 — options.Kind is the options TypeMeta (e.g. "CreateOptions"/"DeleteOptions", or empty), not the resource kind, so the metric and log "kind" labels cannot tell resources apart

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the new logging/metrics labels use `options.Kind` (e.g., `Create`: `d.Log.WithValues("kind", options.Kind, ...)`, similarly for Get/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). In Kubernetes, the `*Options` structs (CreateOptions/DeleteOptions/UpdateOptions/GetOptions/ListOptions) carry TypeMeta fields that are typically empty or describe the options object, not the resource being operated on. The diff shows no other source of the actual resource kind being used, so these "kind" labels are unlikely to distinguish resources as intended. This impacts observability/metrics usefulness rather than functional correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts the bare d.Log into ctx instead of the enriched `log`, dropping name/kind/method from downstream and legacy-goroutine logs

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Async legacy goroutines (also lines 110, 135, 163) derive their context from the request ctx, which is canceled when the handler returns, so legacy writes are likely aborted with context canceled; needs context.WithoutCancel(ctx).

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the new async legacy writes in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection spawn goroutines that call context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) using the request-scoped parent ctx (e.g., `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, ...) }()`). Because that derived context is canceled when the handler returns (common for request contexts), the goroutine’s legacy operation can be immediately aborted with `context canceled`, causing legacy writes/deletes/updates to be dropped. Detaching via context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (or a background context with copied values) would be needed if the intent is for legacy ops to continue after response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Create records a unified-storage failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, so it attributes the error to the wrong backend.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the error path after `d.Storage.Create(...)` fails calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`, even though the failure occurred in unified storage. This misattributes storage failures to the legacy backend (it should call `recordStorageDuration` there). The same misattribution also appears in `Update`’s storage-error path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Update records a unified-storage failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Update, the code measures the unified-storage (d.Storage.Update) call using startStorage, but on error it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of recording a storage/unified-store duration. This mismaps a unified-store failure into legacy metrics, which is a verifiable defect in the diff (the success path uses d.recordStorageDuration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — The DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records its result with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, which pollutes storage metrics with legacy timings and errors.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, within DeleteCollection’s legacy write goroutine, the code measures `startLegacy := time.Now()` and calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`, but then records the result via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. This will incorrectly attribute legacy timings/errors to storage metrics, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Successful Delete passes the object name instead of options.Kind as the kind label, giving the wrong label and unbounded metric cardinality.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, after a successful Storage.Delete, the metrics call uses the object `name` where other methods pass `options.Kind`: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. This would label the metric with per-object names instead of kind, producing incorrect kind labels and potentially unbounded metric cardinality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:134 — Each write starts its own unordered fire-and-forget legacy goroutine, so back-to-back operations on one object (create then delete, update then update) can reach legacy out of order and leave it permanently diverged.

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are now executed asynchronously via `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection(...) }()` after the storage operation returns (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). There is no per-object ordering/serialization between these goroutines, so two back-to-back operations on the same object can race and apply to legacy in a different order than storage (e.g., `Create` returns, caller immediately `Delete`s; the legacy delete goroutine may run before the legacy create goroutine, and then the late legacy create can resurrect the object). This can leave legacy permanently divergent from storage based purely on scheduling/timing, which is a real correctness/data-consistency defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Removing updateWrapper means Legacy.Update re-runs the original objInfo (patch/apply transformers and admission) against legacy's own old object instead of writing the object unified storage persisted, so the two stores can diverge.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the previous Update path computed a single updated object and used updateWrapper to force both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update to apply the same already-computed/returned object (and in the legacy call, it wrapped with the US-returned object). This diff removes that wrapper and now calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` in a goroutine after `d.Storage.Update(...)` succeeds. That means Legacy.Update will be free to re-run `objInfo` against legacy’s own prior state (and any transformers/admission-like logic inside UpdatedObjectInfo), so the object written to legacy can differ from what unified storage persisted, causing divergence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts the bare d.Log into ctx instead of the enriched log, dropping name/kind/method from downstream logging.
matched_golden_ids: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out that Delete stores d.Log in the context instead of the enriched log, causing name/kind/method context values to be lost downstream—same issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Legacy write errors in the async goroutines (also lines 112, 139, 165) are never logged, only counted in a metric, so legacy/unified divergence is silent (the previous code logged them).

adjudication.rationale: In the updated mode3 implementation, legacy writes are performed asynchronously in goroutines for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection. In those goroutines, errors from legacy operations are only passed into `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` (and in DeleteCollection even `d.recordStorageDuration(...)`), but there is no `log.Error(...)` or equivalent logging on failure. The prior synchronous code path explicitly logged legacy failures (e.g., `log.WithValues(...).Error(err, "could not delete from legacy store")`). This is a diff-verifiable observability regression that can make legacy/unified divergence silent, but it doesn't directly prove a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:101 — Delete no longer tolerates NotFound from unified storage, so it skips the legacy delete and leaves legacy-only objects orphaned (the previous code continued to the legacy delete).

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, the new code returns immediately on any error from d.Storage.Delete ("if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }") and only triggers the legacy delete in a goroutine after a successful unified-store delete. The previous implementation explicitly tolerated apierrors.IsNotFound(err) from the unified store and still proceeded to attempt the legacy delete. With the new logic, a NotFound from unified storage prevents legacy deletion, potentially leaving legacy-only objects undeleted (orphaned) as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:38 — The metrics "kind" label uses options.Kind (the Create/Update/DeleteOptions TypeMeta, usually empty), not the resource kind, so the label is effectively meaningless.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3 the code consistently uses `options.Kind` (from `metav1.CreateOptions`, `UpdateOptions`, `DeleteOptions`) and `options.Kind`/`listOptions.Kind` (from list/get options) as the "kind" value in logging and metric recording calls (e.g., `Create`: `d.Log.WithValues("kind", options.Kind, ...)` and `d.recordStorageDuration(..., options.Kind, ...)`). These option structs typically have empty `TypeMeta` unless explicitly populated by the caller, so the resulting "kind" label/value is likely empty or unreliable, making the metric label effectively meaningless. This is a real, diff-grounded observability/metrics-quality issue rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:40 — The "unified store fails" Create case sets up the failure through setupLegacyFn and only passes because legacy and storage share one mock; no mode-3 test waits for or asserts the async legacy call.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestMode3_Create`, the failing case configures `setupLegacyFn` with `m.On("Create", ..., failingObj, ...)` but does not configure `setupStorageFn`. Because both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` are constructed with the same `*mock.Mock` (`m`), the expectation will be matched by the *storage* call (`d.Storage.Create(...)`) as well, so the test can pass without explicitly asserting the unified-store failure path. Also, mode-3 `Create` now performs the legacy write asynchronously in a goroutine with a timeout (`go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`), and none of the mode-3 tests wait for or assert that this async legacy call occurred, making the tests unable to verify the new async behavior and potentially flaky depending on scheduling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Create's Storage-failure path calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration (copy-paste drift in per-method timing boilerplate).

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create(), the timer startStorage is taken before calling d.Storage.Create(...). On the error path, it logs and then calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) even though the operation that failed/timed was the Storage create. This is inconsistent with the success path (which calls recordStorageDuration) and with other methods’ storage error paths, indicating a copy/paste drift that will record incorrect metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Update's Storage-failure path calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, same copy-paste drift as Create.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Update() measures startStorage := time.Now() and calls d.Storage.Update(...). On the error path, it records d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) even though the failure occurred in Storage and the timing startStorage corresponds to the Storage call. This is verifiably inconsistent with the success path (which uses recordStorageDuration) and will misattribute storage failures/latencies to legacy metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — DeleteCollection's async legacy goroutine records recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy timings show up under the storage metric.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go DeleteCollection(), the async goroutine performing the legacy call uses `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` after `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`. This clearly records legacy timings under the storage metric instead of using `recordLegacyDuration`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Delete success path passes `name` as the kind label where every other call site passes options.Kind (inconsistent label, unbounded cardinality).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts d.Log rather than the enriched `log` into ctx, unlike every other method, so downstream loggers lose name/kind/method.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the code builds an enriched logger `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then sets the context with `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` (base logger) rather than `log`. This is inconsistent with other methods in the same diff (e.g., `Create`, `Get`, `List`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`) which put the enriched logger into the context. adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Async legacy goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) drop the legacy error without logging it; the old code logged legacy failures, so only a boolean metric remains for debugging.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes are now done in goroutines for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection and the returned legacy error is only used to call recordLegacyDuration(...), with no log.Error call (e.g., Create: `_, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(...)` then `d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...)`; Delete: `_, _, err := d.Legacy.Delete(...)` then record; Update: `_, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(...)` then record; DeleteCollection: `_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` then record). The prior synchronous implementation logged legacy failures (and in Delete ignored NotFound but logged other errors). This is an observability/debuggability regression but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Magic `time.Second*10` legacy timeout is repeated in four goroutines instead of a named constant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `time.Second*10` repeated in multiple goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection), but this is a maintainability/style nit (use a named constant) rather than a correctness/security/behavior defect or an important non-bug issue evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:134 — The goroutine+timeout+timing block is copy-pasted four times, and startLegacy/defer cancel ordering already differs (Update puts defer cancel after startLegacy, Delete/DeleteCollection start the timer before creating the ctx); extract a helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows repeated, very similar goroutine blocks that wrap legacy writes with `context.WithTimeoutCause(...10s...)`, take a `startLegacy := time.Now()`, call a legacy method, and then record duration. This pattern appears in `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`. The ordering is indeed inconsistent across them (e.g., `Create` creates the timeout ctx then starts the timer; `Delete`/`DeleteCollection` start the timer before creating the timeout ctx; `Update` defers `cancel()` after starting the timer). This is a concrete maintainability issue grounded in the diff and supports the suggestion to extract a helper, but it is not a clear correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:35 — Docstrings (lines 23, 35, 146) still describe synchronous dual writes to LegacyStorage and Storage and never mention the fire-and-forget async legacy write with timeout; Delete (line 94) has no docstring at all.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the comments still describe Mode3/Create/Update as synchronous dual writes (e.g., “writes to LegacyStorage and Storage” and “writes first to Storage and then to LegacyStorage”), but the diff changes Legacy operations to fire-and-forget goroutines with context.WithTimeoutCause (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection spawn a goroutine and return immediately). This is a real, diff-grounded documentation mismatch, and Delete lacks a docstring entirely in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:59 — Returns `created, err` (and `res, async, err` at 116/143) when err is always nil at that point, which hides the fact that legacy errors can never surface.

adjudication.rationale: In the updated Mode3 implementation, returning `created, err` (and `res, async, err`) after the unified-store operation is not a verifiable defect in itself: at that point `err` is the result of the Storage call and will be nil on the success path by construction. Legacy writes are intentionally performed asynchronously in a goroutine (with timeout) and their errors are not propagated to the caller at all. This “legacy errors can never surface” behavior is explicit in the diff and was effectively already true before (legacy errors were logged but not returned), so the finding’s framing as a problem with the return value is not grounded as a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:37 — Per-method `var method = "..."` should be a const, and method naming is inconsistent ("delete-collection" label vs "legacy deletecollection timeout" cause).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show per-method `var method = "..."` assignments (e.g., in `Create`, `Get`, `List`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`) and the strings differ (`"delete-collection"` vs timeout cause `"legacy deletecollection timeout"`). However, this is purely a stylistic consistency/naming nit: using `var` vs `const` for local strings is not a correctness defect, and the timeout-cause string is not used as the method label (the `method` variable is). Nothing in the diff indicates this causes broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:145 — The List test case name still says the store "is not implemented" even though List is now implemented.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is factually true: in `TestMode3_List` one test case is named `"error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented"` even though `DualWriterMode3.List` is now implemented in `dualwriter_mode3.go`. However, this is only a misleading test case description string and does not affect behavior or correctness, making it a minor wording/style nit rather than a substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:119 — TestMode3_Get shadows the package-level `p` registry with a local prometheus.NewRegistry(), the same pattern this change removed from mode1_test and one no other mode3 test uses.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, TestMode3_Get declares a local `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` right before `NewDualWriter(Mode3, ls, us, p)`, which does shadow any package-level `p` used elsewhere in the file/package. The diff also shows the same local-registry pattern being removed from dualwriter_mode1_test.go while still passing `p` into `NewDualWriter`, making this an inconsistent leftover and potentially something a shadowing linter would flag. It’s not a functional defect on its own, but it’s a specific, diff-grounded review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:40 — The unified-store failure case configures its error through setupLegacyFn; because legacy and storage share one mock.Mock, the setup names are misleading and the tests cannot tell which store was called.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go TestMode3_Create, the "error when creating object in the unified store fails" case sets the Create() expectation in setupLegacyFn (m.On("Create", ..., failingObj, ...).Return(nil, error)) while not setting up setupStorageFn. Because both legacyStoreMock and storageMock wrap the same *mock.Mock and both methods are named "Create", the expectation will also match Storage.Create calls, so the test cannot distinguish whether legacy or unified storage was invoked and the helper naming is misleading. This is a test correctness/clarity issue rather than a production defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:337 — Tests never wait for or assert the async legacy goroutine calls, so the new async-legacy-write behavior is unverified and goroutines can outlive the test.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Mode3 operations (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) now perform the legacy write in a background goroutine (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create/... }()`). In the new tests in pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, expectations for legacy calls are set up via `m.On("Create"/"Update"/...)`, but the tests never wait for the goroutine to run nor assert that those legacy expectations were satisfied (e.g., no synchronization and no `m.AssertExpectations(t)`/call counts). This means the async legacy-write behavior is effectively unverified and the legacy goroutine may still be running when the subtest returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: go.work.sum:408 — go.work.sum churn is unrelated to the change (azure-sdk, alertmanager, old otel v0.37/v0.39 entries) and re-adds the pkg/apimachinery go.mod line already present at line 404.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows go.work.sum gained several new module sum entries (e.g., github.com/grafana/grafana-azure-sdk-go/v2 v2.1.0, github.com/grafana/prometheus-alertmanager ..., go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/prometheus v0.37.0, go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric v0.39.0) and it also re-adds an identical `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery .../go.mod` line that already exists a few lines above (line ~404) resulting in a duplicate. While this is not a runtime defect, it is verifiable diff-grounded churn/noise in the dependency sum file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Async legacy writes derive their context from the request ctx, which is canceled as soon as the handler returns, so legacy Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection (lines 51, 110, 135, 163) are routinely aborted and the 10s timeout never effectively applies (use context.WithoutCancel).

adjudication.rationale: In Mode3, Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection start a goroutine for legacy writes and derive the legacy context via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...), where ctx is the request-scoped ctx passed into the method (and further wrapped with klog.NewContext). Since the method returns immediately after launching the goroutine, the request context is typically canceled when the handler completes, which would routinely abort the legacy operation before the 10s timeout is meaningful. This behavior is directly shown in the new async blocks in dualwriter_mode3.go.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:56 — Legacy write errors in all goroutines (56, 113, 140, 166) are silently dropped with no log (previous code logged them) and never retried or reconciled, so the stores diverge with no signal beyond a metric.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes are now performed in goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) and the goroutine bodies record durations but do not log errors (e.g., Create: legacy Create result stored in errObjectSt, then only d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...) is called). Previously, legacy write failures were logged (e.g., Create: log.WithValues(...).Error(...), Delete: log.WithValues(...).Error(...), Update: log.Error(...), DeleteCollection: log.WithValues(...).Error(...)). This is a clear observability regression grounded in the diff, but it doesn’t by itself prove a functional correctness defect (the code intentionally doesn’t fail the request on legacy-write failure).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Background goroutines have no recover(), so a panic in a legacy storage call is outside the apiserver panic-recovery handler and crashes the whole server process.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces background goroutines for legacy writes in Mode3 (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now do `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection(...) }()`). None of these goroutines wrap the legacy call with a `defer recover()` (or otherwise handle panics). In Go, an unrecovered panic in any goroutine terminates the entire process, and the apiserver request-level panic recovery (which would only apply to the request goroutine) would not catch a panic occurring in these new background goroutines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:108 — Fire-and-forget legacy writes have no per-object ordering, so back-to-back requests (e.g. create then delete, or two updates) can apply out of order in legacy storage and leave it permanently inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy operations for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection were changed from synchronous calls to fire-and-forget goroutines (e.g., Create launches `go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, Delete launches `go func(){ d.Legacy.Delete(...) }()`, Update similarly). There is no per-object serialization or ordering mechanism, so successive requests on the same object can execute in legacy storage out of order (e.g., Create’s legacy goroutine may run after a subsequent Delete’s legacy goroutine), leaving the legacy store in a state that does not match unified storage. This risk is directly introduced/exposed by the async legacy writes shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Legacy Update now re-evaluates the raw request-scoped objInfo (patch/admission callbacks and validation funcs) against legacy state after the request completes, instead of the updateWrapper holding the object persisted in unified storage, so legacy can persist different content or fail.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go Update, the previous implementation computed the updated object once (via objInfo.UpdatedObject against the storage-fetched old object), then used an updateWrapper so both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update operated on the same already-materialized object (and Legacy could not re-run request-scoped callbacks to produce different content). The new code calls d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...) and then asynchronously calls d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...) with the raw objInfo again, allowing legacy to re-evaluate UpdatedObject/validation/admission logic against legacy state and potentially write different content or fail even though unified storage succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:101 — Delete now returns early on a NotFound from unified storage (previously tolerated), so objects that exist only in legacy storage are never deleted there, and legacy NotFound is now counted as an error.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete now returns immediately on any error from d.Storage.Delete (including NotFound): `if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }`. Previously it explicitly tolerated `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` from unified storage and still attempted `d.Legacy.Delete(...)`, allowing cleanup of objects that exist only in legacy storage. Also, the new async legacy delete records `err != nil` as an error via `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)` with no NotFound exception, whereas the previous code ignored legacy NotFound errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Unified-storage Create failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, so storage error metrics are wrong and legacy error metrics are inflated.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create, the timing variable is startStorage and the failing call is d.Storage.Create(...). However, on error it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of d.recordStorageDuration(...). This would misattribute unified storage create failures to legacy metrics, inflating legacy error/duration stats and underreporting storage failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Unified-storage Update failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, so failure metrics are attributed to the wrong store.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the error path after `d.Storage.Update(...)` logs "unable to update in storage" but then calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. Since the failure occurred in unified storage (`Storage.Update`), this should be recorded via `recordStorageDuration`, not `recordLegacyDuration`, otherwise metrics are attributed to the wrong store.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — The legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded with recordStorageDuration, so legacy failures show up as unified-storage metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection, the async legacy path records its duration via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` (inside the `go func()`), even though it is timing `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`. This misattributes legacy failures/durations as unified-storage (storage) metrics; it should call `recordLegacyDuration` instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Successful Delete records the object name as the kind label instead of options.Kind, which creates unbounded Prometheus label cardinality.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete(), after a successful unified-store delete, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing `name` in the position used elsewhere for `options.Kind` (e.g., other methods pass `options.Kind`). If that parameter is used as the Prometheus `kind` label, this would incorrectly label by object name, causing unbounded label cardinality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:173 — Destroy tears down Legacy storage without waiting for in-flight legacy goroutines, and goroutine spawning has no bound or backpressure, so pending legacy writes are lost or run against destroyed storage on shutdown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces fire-and-forget goroutines for legacy operations in Mode3 (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection all wrap Legacy.* calls in `go func(){...}()` with no semaphore/worker pool/backpressure), so unbounded concurrent requests can spawn unbounded goroutines. However, the claim that `Destroy` “tears down Legacy storage without waiting” and therefore causes lost writes or calls into destroyed storage cannot be verified from the shown diff, because the `Destroy()` body is not included/changed here. The shutdown/lost-write risk is plausible given the new async behavior, but not strictly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts d.Log into the context instead of the enriched log, so downstream and legacy logs lose the name, kind, and method fields.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, an enriched logger is created (`log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`), but the context is set with the base logger instead (`ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`). As a result, downstream calls (`d.Storage.Delete`, and the legacy goroutine using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`) will not see the enriched fields in `klog.FromContext(ctx)`, so the added name/kind/method metadata is effectively dropped for context-based logging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:110 — Legacy and unified mocks share one *mock.Mock with identical method names, so the "only in unified store" Get/List/Delete tests would still pass if Mode3 read from or wrote to LegacyStorage instead; no AssertNotCalled or per-store distinction exists.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go the tests construct both ls := legacyStoreMock{m, l} and us := storageMock{m, s} using the same shared *mock.Mock (m := &mock.Mock{}). The Get/List/Delete tests typically set expectations only via m.On("Get"/"List"/"Delete", ...) without any AssertNotCalled/expectations to ensure the *other* store was not invoked. Given identical method names on the shared mock, these tests do not clearly distinguish whether DualWriter called Storage vs Legacy, weakening their ability to catch an implementation that mistakenly reads/writes via Legacy in Mode3.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:65 — The async legacy goroutines in Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection are never awaited or asserted (no AssertExpectations, AssertCalled, or Eventually), so removing the legacy write entirely would not fail any test.

adjudication.rationale: In the updated Mode3 implementation, legacy writes in Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection are dispatched in background goroutines (e.g., `go func() { d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`). In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the tests set up `mock.Mock` expectations (e.g., `m.On("Create"...)`, `m.On("Update"...)`) but never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, `AssertCalled`, or any `Eventually`/wait to ensure the async legacy goroutine actually runs before the test ends. Also, several tests (Delete/DeleteCollection) don’t even set legacy expectations at all. As a result, removing the legacy call paths would not necessarily fail these tests, so the finding is valid as a test gap rather than a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — The legacy goroutines derive their context from the request ctx, which is cancelled once the handler returns, but every test passes context.Background(), so legacy writes being cancelled after the response goes untested.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes are now performed asynchronously (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection start `go func()`), and each goroutine derives its context via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` from the caller-provided `ctx`. If a real handler supplies a request-scoped context that is cancelled when the request completes, these background legacy operations could be cancelled early. The added/updated tests invoke these methods with `context.Background()` (e.g., TestMode3_Create/Get/List/Delete/DeleteCollection/Update), so they don't exercise or detect cancellation behavior of request-scoped contexts for the async legacy goroutines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:74 — In the Create and Update success cases both stores return exampleObj (RV "1"), so the assertions can't tell whether the returned object came from Storage or Legacy (Mode1 uses exampleObjNoRV for this).

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the success setups for both `TestMode3_Create` and `TestMode3_Update` have Storage and Legacy mocks returning the same `exampleObj`, and the assertions only check properties/equality against `exampleObj` (or inequality vs `anotherObj`). Given that, the tests don’t actually distinguish/verify that the returned object is specifically the Storage result (even though the implementation currently returns Storage’s result and does Legacy in a goroutine). This is a specific test-strength issue, not a functional bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:38 — No test covers a legacy-side failure or timeout (the response should be unaffected and a legacy error metric recorded); both error cases only cover the unified store failing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds significant new Mode3 behavior where legacy writes are executed asynchronously in goroutines with a 10s timeout cause and metrics recording (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now `go func(){ ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(...); ... d.recordLegacyDuration(...) }()`). The new tests in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go` only assert unified-store outcomes and only include error cases where the unified store returns an error (e.g., Get/List/Delete/DeleteCollection/Update `setupStorageFn` returning `errors.New("error")`). There is no test case that makes the legacy call fail or time out while unified store succeeds, nor any assertion that the response is unaffected and legacy-error metrics are recorded, so the finding is grounded in what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — No test checks metrics, and several labels are wrong without any test failing: storage failures are recorded as legacy duration (:45, :129), the DeleteCollection legacy call is recorded as storage (:166), and Delete passes name as kind (:106).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple concrete metrics-recording mistakes in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`: (1) `Create` records a storage error via `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` (should be storage) in the `if err != nil` block after `d.Storage.Create`; (2) `Update` similarly records a storage error via `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` when `d.Storage.Update` fails; (3) `DeleteCollection`’s legacy delete goroutine calls `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`; and (4) `Delete` success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)`, passing `name` where the kind label is expected (elsewhere it uses `options.Kind`). The added tests do not assert metrics, so these defects would not be caught by them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:101 — Behavior change with no test: Delete now returns early on a unified-store NotFound and skips the legacy delete (the old code tolerated NotFound and still deleted from legacy).

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the new code returns immediately on *any* error from `d.Storage.Delete` (`if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }`), so a unified-store `NotFound` will skip the legacy delete entirely. The previous implementation explicitly tolerated `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` from unified store and still attempted `d.Legacy.Delete`, tolerating legacy `NotFound` as well. This is a verifiable behavior regression that can leave objects orphaned in legacy storage when unified store reports `NotFound`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:138 — Update no longer passes the storage-updated object to legacy through updateWrapper, and the test mocks ignore objInfo, so legacy and unified contents can drift without any test noticing.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, the previous Update implementation computed the updated object once (via objInfo.UpdatedObject against the Storage-fetched old object) and then wrapped objInfo with updateWrapper so the Legacy.Update would apply the same already-updated object. The new code calls d.Storage.Update(...) and then asynchronously calls d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...) without wrapping/pinning the storage-updated object. That means Legacy.Update may recompute a different update based on legacy state, allowing unified-store and legacy contents to diverge. The new tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go also mock Update with mock.Anything for the objInfo argument, so they wouldn’t detect this drift.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:191 — The new mode-3 integration subtests read back only through the k8s/dual-writer path (with FlagKubernetesPlaylists the legacy /api/playlists routes via k8s), so nothing checks that the async legacy SQL writes actually happened.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go the newly added mode-3 subtests (e.g., "with dual write (file, mode 3)" and "with dual write (unified storage, mode 3)") only invoke doPlaylistTests(...) with DualWriterDesiredModes set to Mode3 and FlagKubernetesPlaylists enabled, but the added test code itself contains no assertions/verification that legacy writes occurred. This matters because the mode-3 dual-writer implementation performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines with timeouts (pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go: Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection), so failures/delays in the legacy path could go undetected if tests only validate the primary storage behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:40 — The case "error when creating object in the unified store fails" sets only setupLegacyFn and passes only because the mock is shared, which makes the test misleading and fragile.

adjudication.rationale: In TestMode3_Create, the case "error when creating object in the unified store fails" only configures tt.setupLegacyFn (m.On("Create", ... failingObj ...).Return(...)) and does not configure tt.setupStorageFn, yet the code under test calls Storage.Create first. Because both legacyStoreMock and storageMock are constructed with the same *mock.Mock (m), the single "Create" expectation can satisfy the Storage.Create call (and legacy is not called on early return), so the test can pass while its setup name/intent implies legacy behavior. This is misleading and makes the test fragile to implementation changes, but it’s a test-quality issue rather than a production defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:145 — The List error case is named "...is not implemented", which is stale now that List is implemented.

adjudication.rationale: The test case name in `TestMode3_List` is indeed stale: it says "...is not implemented" even though `DualWriterMode3.List` is implemented in `dualwriter_mode3.go` (previous TODO removed). However, this is only a wording/naming nit in the test and does not indicate a functional defect or substantive review issue grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:289 — The etcd mode-3 integration subtest is unconditionally skipped, so it adds no coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go the newly added subtest `t.Run("with dual write (etcd, mode 3)", ...)` calls `t.Skip("local etcd testing")` unconditionally at the start of the subtest body, so none of the mode-3 etcd test logic (helper setup, DeleteCollection, `doPlaylistTests`) will ever execute in CI. This means the added subtest provides no additional coverage.
